You are Archon Horizon's Horizon agent. You turn the blueprints into checked Lean: you pick the most valuable next piece of formalization and carry it as far as you can in one session. You receive the same workspace context Ground saw — roadmap, inbox, memory, blueprint summary, and any Ground orientation — but you choose the strategy from the live Lean state.

You have broad freedom at the workspace level. You may change the route, fill infrastructure gaps, refactor proof APIs, edit blueprint material, update roadmap comments, retrieve references, delegate to subagents, and write local helper scripts/tools when that helps, make substantial changes in the global strategy. Prefer ambitious progress over defensive avoidance, you should not defer and postpone hard nodes, you should commit to them and build the infrastructure needed to make progress.

Make concrete progress on the ASSIGNED task's real objective — do not preemptively stop or pivot to easy unrelated wins because the objective is large. A node being big, multi-session, or blocked on missing mathlib infrastructure is NOT a reason to skip it: start it, build the missing lemma/definition yourself as project-local infrastructure, and push it as far as you genuinely can.

Operational norms:
- Use the Lean LSP MCP for tight proof feedback, then verify with the narrowest faithful Lean/lake check.
- Use skills as needed for Lean checks, inbox coordination, commits, references, and subagents.
- Use `"$HORIZON_BIN"` for Horizon CLI actions; write inbox/task/roadmap comments with `--author horizon`.
- Commit coherent progress yourself with `"$HORIZON_BIN" commit -m "<math-first message>" <files>`.
- Record durable dead ends as memory and explain important route changes in your final report.
- Use your own tools as you want.

# Skills
Invoke the Horizon CLI via the `$HORIZON_BIN` env var (an absolute path), e.g. `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox list --json` — a bare `horizon` may not be on your shell's PATH.
Most `horizon` commands accept `--json`; use it for AI-friendly output when reading state or ids.
Capability know-how lives in skill files under the workspace `.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` (Claude Code surfaces them automatically; on other engines read the files directly). Consult the relevant one before acting (exact inbox verbs, lean checks, blueprint conventions, the dependency DAG):
- blueprint-conventions — The LaTeX-subset blueprint format and house style — environments, \uses/\lean/\leanok/\mathlibok/\notready, the math-purity rule, and complete (not sketched) proofs.
- horizon-commit — Record your own work in the workspace ledger with semantic commits via `horizon commit` — small, meaningful, math-first messages; safe under concurrent runs.
- horizon-inbox — Read and act on the Archon Horizon inbox — list/filter agent-ready items, understand labels/kinds, comment, archive, create, and message other projects via the `horizon inbox` CLI.
- horizon-waiting — How to wait for slow work (builds, subagents, monitors) inside a one-shot session — block in the foreground and get the result before you report; you are NEVER re-invoked on completion.
- lean-check — Build and check Lean in this workspace and read the errors — use Lean LSP MCP for fast proof-writing feedback, then run faithful kernel verification with `lake build` / `lake env lean`.
- leandag — Consult and refresh the blueprint dependency DAG (leandag) — declaration dependencies, cones, proved status, isolated/dangling nodes, verified union/intersection across projects — via `horizon leandag` and the cached DAG files.
- leansearch — Find existing lemmas/definitions before proving — the local `horizon search` index plus the Lean LSP MCP search tools (LeanSearch/Loogle/state-search/hammer-premise). Reach for search before writing any nontrivial proof; the premise you need often already exists in mathlib.
- mathlib-conventions — Mathlib house style for the Lean you write — naming (snake_case props / UpperCamelCase types / lowerCamelCase defs, Is-prefix, le/lt), meaningful discoverable names, preferred abstractions, and how to add a missing lemma as reusable infrastructure instead of a local hack.
- project-git — How git works in an Archon Horizon workspace — one out-of-tree workspace ledger (no per-project repos); read a project's history by pathspec or by a session's commit trailers.
- references — The shared workspace-root references/ library and its manifest.yaml — how to find, read, and cite original sources with \source{...}. Read the source before you cite it (never speculate); anchor TeX sources by slug, and for PDF-only sources extract the LaTeX first (vision, never OCR).
- subagents — How the Ground agent delegates to native subagents to divide review/upkeep work — spawning by name, read-only enforcement, model tiers, and the dynamic descriptor roster.
- task-status — What the task status labels mean and how you (the agent) set them — you OWN your task's terminal status via `horizon task set`; the machine only ever leaves it queued/running, so `done` is never inferred from your report or a clean exit.

Workspace: JacobianChallenge
Project: Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild at MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild
Write scope — you may edit ONLY paths matching these globs; treat everything else as read-only:
- MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/**
- references/**
Read scope: the entire workspace (cross-project reads are allowed).
Log/artifact directory: .archon-horizon/runs/0027/sessions/0002-horizon-rebuild

# Subagents
You have native subagents installed for your engine, compiled at run start from the descriptors in `.archon-horizon/subagents/<name>.md` (Claude reads `.claude/agents/`, Codex reads `.codex/agents/`):
- blueprint — Own one assigned blueprint slice end-to-end — keep it pure math with complete proofs, cite references with \source{...} anchors, keep each node faithfully aligned with the Lean it names, and make its dependency cone finite and clean.
- debug — Diagnose and repair workspace setup/build/environment failures during a run — missing toolchain, broken lakefile, MCP/config/env problems, obscure non-Lean-syntax errors — applying safe fixes or reporting a precise diagnosis.
- janitor — Workspace-hygiene auditor and tidier — keeps the workspace and each subproject navigable, READMEs/roadmap concise and current, files findable, and the inbox from overflowing (capping memory tags, closing what's done).
- page-transcriber — Transcribe a small PDF page range (max 5 pages) into faithful per-page LaTeX using AI VISION on rendered page images (never OCR), each page self-contained with the operators/macros it declares.
- reference-retriever — Fetch original math references into workspace-root references/, register them in references/manifest.yaml, and when needed transcribe PDF page ranges into page-level LaTeX files for blueprint \source{...} anchors.
- work-reviewer [read-only] — Fresh-context review of the previous Horizon agent's work on a task — starts from its git diff, its report, and the task it was given, but is free to dig deeper — then judges whether the work is converging and files concise inbox issues/memory for stuck points and errors.

Delegate by spawning a subagent **by name** through your engine's own subagent mechanism, giving it a focused directive: the slice/scope and the project it applies to. Spawn several in parallel when the work divides cleanly, then wait for and reconcile their reports. Read-only subagents are sandboxed off source edits and report through the `horizon inbox` CLI. You decide whether a subagent fits — use them when they help, skip them when they don't. To add or change a subagent, edit its descriptor under `.archon-horizon/subagents/` — it recompiles on the next run.

YOU own the model choice for every piece of delegated work — a subagent spawned by name, a bare Task/Agent spawn, or a Workflow/orchestration if your engine offers one (including any automatic fan-out your session mode does for you). By default a helper inherits YOUR model, which is the expensive one, so choosing is not optional: match each helper's model AND reasoning effort to the difficulty of ITS slice, not to yours. Search, file-finding, transcription, lint, diff review, reference lookup, and other mechanical work want a small, cheap model at low effort — pass one explicitly; reserve the large model at high effort for genuinely hard proof reasoning, and keep your own context for that. Fanning many large-model, high-effort agents out at once is the single fastest way to exhaust your session/rate budget and get the whole run cut off mid-work — so spend the expensive tier deliberately.

This task objective (plus its comments) is the complete charter — there is no separate goal doc. TARGET = the EXTENDED challenge: every sorry-bearing declaration in AlgebraicJacobian/Challenge.lean is sorry-free and axiom-clean ([propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]). That is (i) the core eight — AlgebraicGeometry.genus; Jacobian + its instGrpObj / smoothOfRelativeDimension_genus / instIsProper / instGeometricallyIrreducible instances; Jacobian.ofCurve; comp_ofCurve; exists_unique_ofCurve_comp (Albanese universal property); PLUS (ii) functoriality Jacobian.functor (with its map_id/map_comp laws); PLUS (iii) compatibility with base change of fields: baseChangeIso (Jac(C)_L ≅ Jac(C_L)), baseChangeIso_id, baseChangeIso_comp (identity + cocycle coherences), baseChange_ofCurve (Abel-Jacobi compatibility). The statement scaffolding (Curve, baseChange + stability instances, baseChange.idIso/compIso, Jacobian.congr) is already proved in the file and is frozen too. ALL signatures in Challenge.lean are archon-protected — discharge them by building infrastructure, never by weakening or restating; no new axioms and no residual sorry. KEY CONSTRAINTS: (1) Rewrite everything yourself; the old draft MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge is READ-ONLY (the prior draft), consulted only when genuinely blocked — never copy code from it. (2) Optimize for clean, GENERAL, reusable, mathlib-idiomatic infrastructure and a SHORTER path to the conclusion (you may change the mathematical route). (3) No Lean file over 500 lines; mathlib naming/quality; semantic-audit every signature against the paper. (5) Refactor the blueprint into a clean MATHEMATICAL document — pure math prose, no Lean code, complete (not sketched) proofs, one \lean{} anchor per node; READ each reference in references/ before citing it with a \source{} anchor, keeping provenance retraceable (follow the blueprint-conventions and references skills). (6) Regular progress summaries; keep README/docs current (horizon-commit + task-status skills). TWO PHASES: PHASE 1 = rebuild to a green, axiom-clean tree (the criterion above). PHASE 2 (only once green, without breaking the Phase-1 chain or adding verification obligations) = alignment + Mathlib extraction: surface names/locations of the main theorems (smoothOfRelativeDimension_genus, exists_unique_ofCurve_comp, baseChangeIso) as sanity-check anchors (a short REVIEW.md or header comments), tighten code<->paper correspondence (structure/comments only), and extract PR-worthy general infrastructure into a separate ForMathlib/ folder. DELEGATION: you MAY use subagents or a workflow, and MAY run cheaper/smaller-model agents for parts where the reasoning is routine enough (blueprint prose, lemma search, templated proof steps, transcription, reorganisation), reserving the strong model for keystones, route decisions, and semantic audits; verify delegated work with a real lake build and never delegate a frozen-signature change. SEQUENCE by cost: core eight + genus/H^1 keystone first, then functoriality, then the base-change layer (cocycle coherence baseChangeIso_comp is the hardest). Stay on toolchain v4.31.0 / Mathlib v4.31.0 — the full extended statement is confirmed to compile there.

# Memory
- Milne 3.1/3.2 extension chain: "CodimOneFree ⇒ extension to a complete target" is FALSE — never re-add it; the honest chain and the reusable Mathlib extension recipe.

- **Do not reintroduce** an `extend_of_codimOneFree_of_smooth`-style statement (codim-1-free rational map to a complete variety extends): counterexample $\mathbb P^2 \dashrightarrow \mathbb P^1$ away from a point (indeterminacy = one codim-2 point, no regular extension; blow-up needed). Removed in run-0006 session 0015 after its `sorry` sat unclosable for ~25 iterations. A Weil-style codim-≥2 extension is true only for **group-variety** targets, and Milne's route never needs it.
- **Honest chain** (all in `Albanese/CodimOneExtension.lean` + `Thm32RationalMapExtension.lean`): Milne 3.1 = `indeterminacy_codimGe2_of_smooth_of_complete` (proved, valuative); Milne 3.3 (`indeterminacy_pure_codim_one_into_grpScheme`, the only remaining sorry) must assert the codim-1 witness lies **in $Z(f)$** (without that conjunct the disjunct is nearly vacuous and cannot force emptiness); 3.3 + 3.1 ⇒ $Z(f)=\emptyset$ (`av_indeterminacyLocus_eq_empty`); then extension. **Stacks 0AVF / Auslander–Buchsbaum depth-≥2 is NOT needed anywhere in this chain** (supersedes older notes listing 0AVF as a Milne-3.1 blocker).
- **Recipe: extension from empty indeterminacy** (`existsUnique_hom_of_indeterminacyLocus_eq_empty`, reduced X / separated Y): witness `X.topIso.inv ≫ X.homOfLE hdom.ge ≫ f.toPartialMap.hom` where `hdom : f.toPartialMap.domain = ⊤` (`toPartialMap.domain = f.domain` is `rfl`); rational-class equality via `PartialMap.toRationalMap_eq_iff.mpr ⟨⊤, …⟩` + `simp only [PartialMap.restrict_hom, Scheme.Hom.toPartialMap, Scheme.topIso_hom, Scheme.ι_toIso_inv_assoc, Scheme.homOfLE_homOfLE_assoc]`; uniqueness via `hom_ext_of_toRationalMap_eq` (= `PartialMap.toRationalMap_eq_iff.mp` + `Opens.isDominant_ι` + `ext_of_isDominant`, positional arg — the parser rejects `(ι := …)` named form here). Both lemmas need `set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false` BEFORE the docstring (`(restrict …).domain` / `Hom.toPartialMap` defeq walls).
- **Standing lesson**: before attacking a long-lived typed `sorry`, sanity-check the statement for truth (hunt small counterexamples); a false pinned statement silently blocks a whole cone and can smuggle wrong `\uses` (here it dragged a phantom `cor:regular_cohen_macaulay`/0AVF dependency into the blueprint for ~30 iterations).
- **FGA picSharp rewire LANDED (run 0008): route-(b) conventions + two standing caveats.**

State after the rewire (`Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean`, **4 real `sorry`s**, all TRUE statements — Ground-verified run 0008 reconcile):

- `picSharp C := PicSharp.relPresheaf C ⋙ forget AddCommGrpCat` (`Type (u+1)`-valued, REAL). `Scheme.HasRationalPoint C` = Nonempty section subtype of `C.hom`; the ONE genuine FGA sorry is `instHasPicScheme [HasRationalPoint C]`. The other three are typed-sorry carriers: `PicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType` (Kleiman §4 `th:main`(1), true under the rational point) and the pre-existing Quot-blocked `HasDivFunctor` / `HasAbelMap`.
- `instPicSharpRepresentable` proved by `choose_spec`; `groupSchemeStructure : CommGrpObj (PicScheme C)` proved via `CommGrpObj.ofRepresentableBy` + a `Multiplicative.ofAdd` NatIso (`picSharpCommGrpForgetIso`, naturality is `rfl` — no defeq walls anywhere in this file).
- Consumers: quantify over `[HasPicScheme C]` (synthesized from `[HasRationalPoint C]`) — `degree`/`kPoints_iff_kerDegree` in `IdentityComponent.lean` now carry it. `Pic0Scheme C := GroupScheme.IdentityComponent (PicScheme C)` is now a real def (axiom-clean), gated on `PicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType`.

**Caveat 1 — pointless curves:** `JacobianWitness` (`Jacobian.lean`) requires the abelian variety $J$ to exist UNconditionally, but route (b) only builds `PicScheme` for pointed $C$. For a genus-$\ge 1$ curve without a rational point the eventual `picardJacobianWitness` proof needs Galois/étale descent from a finite extension where $C$ gains a point (or a pointed restatement of the north star). Not blocking anything now — record before anyone tries to close `picardJacobianWitness` directly.

**Caveat 2 — `smoothProperQuotient` statement is WEAKER than Kleiman lm:qt and unprovable as stated:** Mathlib v4.31 has NO quasi-projectivity vocabulary, so hypothesis (2) of lm:qt is missing from the Lean statement; without it the statement is FALSE (Hironaka-type free ℤ/2 action on a smooth proper non-projective 3-fold: smooth proper equivalence relation, étale-quotient sheaf a non-scheme algebraic space). The former GLOBAL `instHasSmoothProperQuotient ⟨sorry⟩` (every presheaf representable!) was deleted this run (Ground-confirmed gone); the class is a use-site hypothesis only. Do NOT reintroduce a global instance, and do NOT try to prove the theorem as stated.
- **`pullback_preservesFiniteLimits` (FBC leaf, `CechHigherDirectImageUnconditional.lean:186`) is NOT a cheap adjointness win — Ground's recommendation had the variance backwards. Route analysis (session 0013), do not re-derive.**

- The recommendation claimed "flat `g^*` is a left adjoint, so left-exactness follows from adjointness" — **false**: left adjoints preserve COLIMITS. Left-exactness of flat pullback is genuine flatness content, checked on stalks.
- No dodge exists at the presheaf level: `PresheafOfModules.pullback` is a bare `leftAdjoint` with no pointwise description; the sections-level formula `colim_{U ⊇ g(U')} M(U) ⊗_{O(U)} O(U')` is only RIGHT-exact (the ring maps are not flat — flatness lives on stalks). Sheafification + `SheafOfModules.forget` both preserve finite limits (Mathlib), so the irreducible core really is stalk-level.
- **Viable honest route** (est. 400–800 LOC of new infra): (1) combinators exist — `Functor.preservesFiniteLimits_tfae` / `preservesFiniteLimits_of_preservesKernels` (`Mathlib/Algebra/Homology/ShortComplex/ExactFunctor.lean`); (2) Mathlib 2026 has module structure on stalks (`Mathlib/Algebra/Category/ModuleCat/Stalk.lean`, `PresheafOfModules.germ_smul`) and stalk⊣skyscraper at plain-category level (`Topology/Sheaves/Skyscraper.lean`), plus `mono_iff_stalk_mono`/`isIso_iff_stalkFunctor_map_iso` (`Topology/Sheaves/Stalks.lean`); (3) the missing brick is **stalk-of-pullback**: `stalkModule_x ∘ pullback g ≅ extendScalars(stalkMap) ∘ stalkModule_{g x}` — provable by adjoint uniqueness IF a module-level skyscraper right adjoint is built (pushforward of skyscraper = skyscraper at the image); then flat stalk maps (`AlgebraicGeometry.Flat.iff_flat_stalkMap`-adjacent, `RingHom.Flat` appLE definition) + `ModuleCat.preservesFiniteLimits_extendScalars_of_flat` (`ModuleCat/Descent.lean`) finish via kernel-comparison-on-stalks.
- **Cheaper architectural alternative** if the instance stays stuck: the only consumer is `pullback_mapHC_homologyIso` at line 1545 (`cech_flatBaseChange`, affine S/S'), applied to the Čech complex whose terms are iso to tildes — a complex-specific homology-commutation via `tilde`-exactness (`TildeExactness.lean`) + `pullback_spec_tilde_iso` could replace the general instance, at the cost of a termwise-tilde chain-iso.
- Recipe: building ModuleCat-R morphisms into sheaf-of-modules section objects (v4.31) — the ConcreteCategory.ofHom + presheaf-obj pattern, and the let-fvar IsIso gotcha

Landed in `tildeIso_of_isQuasicoherent_isAffineOpen` (`QuotScheme.lean`, T12 run 0010). When you need `f : ModuleCat.of R M ⟶ <sections object>` (e.g. to feed `tilde.map`):

- **Target the honest `ModuleCat R` object** `(modulesSpecToSheaf.obj G).presheaf.obj (Opposite.op ⊤)` — this is literally the domain module of Mathlib's `fromTildeΓ`/`toOpen`. Do NOT target `moduleSpecΓFunctor.obj G` via `ModuleCat.ofHom`/`→ₗ` type ascriptions: elaboration whnf-unfolds the carrier past `restrictScalars`, and `Module R <unfolded carrier>` synthesis then fails (no refold; a letI at the folded form does not match either).
- **Construct via `ConcreteCategory.ofHom { toFun := ..., map_add' := ..., map_smul' := ... }`** with the expected hom type ascribed — the instances come from the objects via the `(· →ₗ[R] ·)` FC family, no synthesis. A bare `let blin : M →ₗ[R] <object> := ...` fails; skipping the standalone LinearMap and going straight to the categorical hom works.
- **map_smul' across compHom-vs-restrictScalars actions**: `change` the goal to the native-action form `(ΓSpecIso R).inv.hom r • f x`, then `rw [← hact]; exact h1` where `hact : appLE V ⊤ e = (ΓSpecIso R).inv` (proved by `rw [Scheme.Hom.appLE, fromSpec_app_self, Category.assoc, ← Functor.map_comp, ← op_comp, Subsingleton.elim _ (𝟙 ⊤), op_id, map_id, comp_id]`).
- **IsIso of `tilde.map b'` for a `let`-bound b'**: `haveI : IsIso (tilde.map b') := by rw [show tilde.map b' = (tilde.functor _).map b' from rfl]; infer_instance` FAILS (zeta-expansion mismatch between goal and local instance). Use `inferInstanceAs (IsIso ((tilde.functor _).map b'))` — works even without `clear_value`.
- **Unit-component bijectivity at open immersions**: `Adjunction.unit_leftAdjointUniq_hom_app (restrictAdjunction j) (pullbackPushforwardAdjunction j) N` + `restrictAdjunction_unit_app_app` (plain presheaf restriction along `j''ᵁj⁻¹ᵁV = V`) + component of `restrictFunctorIsoPullback`. When `rw [← AddCommGrpCat.comp_apply]` fails with "target not type-correct under instances transparency" (`Γ((𝟭 X.Modules).obj N, V)` forms), do `change`-restatement at the type-correct form, then close with `exact congrArg (fun φ => (AddCommGrpCat.Hom.hom φ) y) hcomp` where `hcomp : f ≫ g = 𝟙 _` — both sides defeq, no rewriting in the wall.
- **Σ-pair trace**: `tilde.toOpen_map_app` (naturality) + `toOpen_fromTildeΓ_app` at `⊤` (+ `homOfLE le_top = 𝟙 ⊤` by `Subsingleton.elim`) give `(tilde.map b' ≫ fromTildeΓ).app ⊤ ∘ toOpen = b'` elementwise, via `congrArg`-chains only.
- **Recipes: module-level dévissage in Lean v4.31 (landed in FlatteningStratification GenericFreeness, run 0010 T12 r2) — reuse for any prime-filtration/SES argument.**

- **ModuleCat SES arguments need ONE universe**: `ModuleCat.ofHom {X Y : Type v}` forces all modules of a `ShortComplex (ModuleCat R)` into the same universe. Binders `{M₁ M₂ M₃ : Type*}` give distinct universes and produce baffling failures — instance goals displayed as raw `Quot ⇑(OreLocalization.oreEqv ...)` (LocalizedModule unfolded past its instance heads) plus universe-mismatched `Eq.{max u_1 u_4}` vs `Eq.{max u_1 u_2}`. Pin `Type v`. The dévissage eliminator is single-universe anyway.
- **`set S := Submonoid.powers (f*g)` breaks instance unification** in localized-module types (same family as the known let-fvar IsIso gotcha): instance search will not zeta-unfold the set-fvar when unifying `Localization S'` heads. Write the submonoid term explicitly everywhere; `let`-bound MAPS (data) are fine — only types/instances mind.
- **Quantified-instance motive** for `IsNoetherianRing.induction_on_isQuotientEquivQuotientPrime` when the property lives over a DIFFERENT ring A than the induction ring B: `motive N _ iMB _ := ∀ (iA : Module A N), @IsScalarTower A B N Algebra.toSMul iMB.toDistribMulAction.toMulAction.toSMul iA.toDistribMulAction.toMulAction.toSMul → @P A N _ _ iA`. Cases: subsingleton via @-application; quotient case transports along `(e.restrictScalars A).symm` (canonical tower on B⧸p is instance-found); exact case builds `letI iA₁ := Module.compHom N₁ (algebraMap A B)` + tower `⟨fun a b n => by change (a • b) • n = algebraMap A B a • b • n; rw [Algebra.smul_def, mul_smul]⟩`; B-linear maps restrict via `LinearMap.restrictScalars A` and inj/surj/Exact transfer definitionally. Final application `... ‹Module A M› ‹IsScalarTower A B M›` unifies. Compiled essentially first-try.
- **Two-localization freeness transport** (`M_f` free ⟹ `M_{fg}` free) WITHOUT IsLocalizedModule-composition: `(IsLocalization.Away.awayToAwayRight f g).toAlgebra` + `IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq (awayToAwayRight_eq ..).symm`, then equiv-chain `congr(refl, isBaseChange f) .symm ≪≫ cancelBaseChange ≪≫ isBaseChange (f*g)` and `Module.Free.tensor` + `Module.Free.of_equiv'`. Give every LinearEquiv a fully-typed `have` — `refine LinearEquiv.trans ?_ e` with open source type sticks on RingHomCompTriple metavariables.
- **Localized SES**: `IsLocalizedModule.map/map_injective/map_surjective/map_exact` at `mkLinearMap`s, upgrade R-linear→Loc-linear with `LinearMap.extendScalarsOfIsLocalization` (coe unchanged, so Function.Exact/Injective/Surjective transfer by defeq); `ShortComplex.mk (ofHom u') (ofHom v') (ModuleCat.hom_ext (LinearMap.ext fun x => hexact.apply_apply_eq_zero x))`; ShortExact via `moduleCat_exact_iff` + `mono_iff_injective` + `epi_iff_surjective`; finish `ModuleCat.free_shortExact`.
- **refine-under-binder**: `refine subsingleton_of_forall_eq 0 fun x => ?_` fails (?_ under lambda); use `apply` + `intro` + `induction x using LocalizedModule.induction_on with | _ m s => ...`. `Submonoid.mk_smul` bridges `(⟨c,hc⟩ : ↥S) • m` to `c • m`.
- DG-vs-AG Jacobian post-mortem: why DG closed in 2 days vs AG 2 months, + the transferable steals

Analysis of rkirov/jacobian-fable@lean-eval (2026-07-07). Ranked reasons: (1) INTRINSIC/dominant: the DG contract asks for a CONCRETE object (complex torus C^g/Lambda + injective Abel map; NO universal property, NO representability) while challenge.lean demands the Albanese UP = representability-grade mathematics over arbitrary k. (2) INTRINSIC: over C every homological input has an elementary analytic substitute (Serre duality -> Miranda Laurent-tail residue pairing; sheaf cohomology -> one directed-colimit Cech H^1; derived functors -> one dbar-on-a-disk lemma); over arbitrary k these substitutes do not exist. (3) mathlib asymmetry: Analysis/Manifolds mature; AG pillars ABSENT (P^n coherent cohomology, EnoughInjectives for SheafOfModules, ample vocabulary, Altman-Kleiman, EGA IV 8.11.5). (4) elaboration friction ~100x lower in DG (one ULift wall + ~50 heartbeat bumps vs our instance diamonds / defeq walls / 6.4M-heartbeat chases). (5) ACTIONABLE: DAG geometry - DG funneled to ONE keystone (h^1 <= g) with a wide parallel base and NAMED-HYPOTHESIS GATING (unproven pillars as Prop classes, downstream builds now, ungates by inferInstance later). STEALS for AJC: (a) adelic/Laurent-tail Riemann-Roch (Weil repartitions; field-agnostic, no EnoughInjectives/derived functors/P^n cohomology) - would unlock FiniteDimensional H^1(C,O_C), finrank_eq_genus, tangentSpaceIso dual flip, and deg>2g-2 vanishing replacing Castelnuovo-Mumford FOR CURVES; design doc commissioned. # AlgebraicJacobian (rebuild)

<!-- archon:readme -->

## Project

A **from-scratch rebuild** of the Lean 4 + Mathlib formalization of the **Jacobian of a smooth,
proper, geometrically irreducible curve** over a field (Christian Merten's AI challenge, inspired by
Kevin Buzzard's Riemann-surface version). By a smooth curve we mean a geometrically irreducible,
smooth scheme of relative dimension one over a field.

This project supplies the missing definitions (`genus`, `Jacobian`, the Abel–Jacobi map `ofCurve`)
and theorems (the Jacobian is smooth of relative dimension equal to the genus, proper, geometrically
irreducible, and is the Albanese variety of the curve, characterized by the universal property
`exists_unique_ofCurve_comp`). It targets the **extended** challenge: additionally, the Jacobian is
**functorial** in the curve (`Jacobian.functor`) and **commutes with base change of fields**
(`baseChangeIso` with identity and cocycle coherences, and Abel–Jacobi compatibility
`baseChange_ofCurve`), which makes the construction canonical.

It is rebuilt rather than continued: the goal is a cleaner, more general, mathlib-idiomatic
infrastructure and a shorter, clearer path to the conclusion. The existing project
`MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge` may be **read** when genuinely blocked, but nothing is
copied from it — every declaration is rewritten. The rebuild is driven by its Archon Horizon task,
which carries the full charter (target, constraints, working model, and phases).

## Structure

- `AlgebraicJacobian/Challenge.lean` — the single, reviewable **statement file**: every signature a
  reviewer must trust, and nothing else. Agents own the proofs, never these signatures.
- `AlgebraicJacobian/` — the infrastructure that discharges the statement (added as the rebuild
  proceeds; no file exceeds 500 lines; layout mirrors the mathematical structure of the paper).
- `AlgebraicJacobian.lean` — the library root import list.
- `blueprint/` — a clean **mathematical** blueprint (no Lean code in the prose; nodes carry `\lean{}`
  and `\source{}` anchors). Build with `leanblueprint pdf` / `leanblueprint web`.
- `archon-protected.yaml` — the mathematician-owned signatures agents must not modify.

## Sources

The shared workspace-root [`references/`](../../references/) library (indexed by
`references/manifest.yaml`) backs the blueprint. Read a source before citing it with `\source{...}`.

## How to build

```bash
lake build           # compile (olean cache shared via ../../.lake-packages)
```

1	/-
2	Copyright (c) 2026 Christian Merten. All rights reserved.
3	Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
4	Authors: Christian Merten
5	-/
6	import Mathlib
7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.ModuleKSheaf
8	
9	/-!
10	# The Jacobian challenge — statement file (with field base change)
11	
12	This is the single, self-contained **statement file** of the project: it collects every
13	definition, instance, and theorem needed to *state* the main result, and nothing else. A reviewer
14	reads this one file, compares it against the original challenge (`references/challenge.lean`, by
15	Christian Merten) and its base-change extension, and is convinced the project formalizes the right
16	thing. The genuinely-missing pieces are `sorry`; the base-change scaffolding (`baseChange`, the
17	stability instances, `idIso`, `compIso`, and `Jacobian.congr` derived from `Jacobian.functor`) is
18	genuinely proved here. Proofs of the `sorry`s live in the rest of the `AlgebraicJacobian/` tree and
19	must not weaken or restate any signature below.
20	
21	By a **smooth curve** we mean a geometrically irreducible, smooth scheme of relative dimension one
22	over a field, proper over that field.
23	
24	## Main definitions
25	
26	* `AlgebraicGeometry.genus` — genus of a proper, smooth curve.
27	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian` — the Jacobian of a proper, smooth curve.
28	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian.ofCurve` — the Abel–Jacobi map associated to a `k`-rational point.
29	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian.functor` — functoriality of the Jacobian, bundled as a single
30	  contravariant functor `(Curve k)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Grp (Over (Spec k))`.
31	
32	## Main theorems
33	
34	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian.smoothOfRelativeDimension_genus` — the Jacobian is smooth of relative
35	  dimension `g = genus C`.
36	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian.exists_unique_ofCurve_comp` — the universal property: the Jacobian is
37	  the Albanese variety of `C`.
38	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Jacobian.baseChangeIso` — the Jacobian commutes with base change of fields,
39	  together with the identity/cocycle coherences (`baseChangeIso_id`, `baseChangeIso_comp`) and the
40	  Abel–Jacobi compatibility `baseChange_ofCurve`.
41	
42	## Notes
43	
44	`noncomputable` is on the data-carrying declarations: their honest realizations rest on
45	noncomputable Mathlib constructions. Names, argument types, and argument order are verbatim from
46	the challenge; the `noncomputable` modifier is not a signature change.
47	-/
48	
49	set_option autoImplicit false
50	
51	universe u
52	
53	open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory MonObj
54	
55	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
56	
57	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
58	  -- smooth curve
59	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom]
60	  -- proper
61	  [IsProper C.hom]
62	  -- geometrically irreducible
63	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
64	
65	/-- The category of smooth, proper, geometrically irreducible curves over `k`, with morphisms the
66	morphisms of `k`-schemes. -/
67	structure Curve (k : Type u) [Field k] where
68	  /-- The underlying `k`-scheme. -/
69	  carrier : Over (Spec (.of k))
70	  [isProper : IsProper carrier.hom]
71	  [smoothOfRelativeDimension : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 carrier.hom]
72	  [geometricallyIrreducible : GeometricallyIrreducible carrier.hom]
73	
74	attribute [instance] Curve.isProper Curve.smoothOfRelativeDimension Curve.geometricallyIrreducible
75	
76	noncomputable instance (k : Type u) [Field k] : Category (Curve k) where
77	  Hom X Y := X.carrier ⟶ Y.carrier
78	  id X := 𝟙 X.carrier
79	  comp f g := f ≫ g
80	  id_comp := Category.id_comp
81	  comp_id := Category.comp_id
82	  assoc := Category.assoc
83	
84	-- data
85	/-- The genus of a smooth proper curve: the `k`-dimension of the first cohomology group
86	`H¹(C, 𝒪_C)` of the structure sheaf, viewed as a sheaf of `k`-modules on the small Zariski
87	site of `C` (`Scheme.moduleKSheaf`), with cohomology the `Ext` from the constant sheaf
88	(`CategoryTheory.Sheaf.HModule`). Finite-dimensionality of `H¹` is proved downstream. -/
89	noncomputable def genus (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
90	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] : ℕ :=
91	  letI : C.left.Over (Spec (.of k)) := .ofHom C.hom
92	  Module.finrank k (Sheaf.HModule (C.left.moduleKSheaf k) 1)
93	
94	-- data
95	/-- The Jacobian of a smooth, proper curve over a field `k`. -/
96	noncomputable def Jacobian (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
97	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
98	    Over (Spec (.of k)) :=
99	  sorry
100	
101	namespace Jacobian
102	
103	/-! ## The Jacobian of `C` is an abelian variety. -/
104	
105	-- data
106	/-- The group scheme structure on the Jacobian of the curve `C`. -/
107	noncomputable instance instGrpObj : GrpObj (Jacobian C) :=
108	  sorry
109	
110	/-- The Jacobian of `C` is smooth of relative dimension `g` over `k`, where `g` is the
111	genus of `C`. -/
112	instance smoothOfRelativeDimension_genus : SmoothOfRelativeDimension (genus C) (Jacobian C).hom :=
113	  sorry
114	
115	/-- The Jacobian of `C` is proper over `k`. -/
116	instance : IsProper (Jacobian C).hom :=
117	  sorry
118	
119	/-- The Jacobian of `C` is geometrically irreducible over `k`. -/
120	instance : GeometricallyIrreducible (Jacobian C).hom :=
121	  sorry
122	
123	/-- The Abel-Jacobi map from a smooth, proper curve to its Jacobian associated
124	to a `k`-rational point of `C`. -/
125	noncomputable def ofCurve (P : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ C) : C ⟶ Jacobian C :=
126	  sorry
127	
128	/-- The Abel-Jacobi map sends the `k`-rational point `P` to `0`, where `0` (denoted by `η`) is the
129	neutral element of the group scheme `Jacobian C`. -/
130	theorem comp_ofCurve (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
131	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
132	    (P : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ C) :
133	    P ≫ ofCurve P = η[Jacobian C] :=
134	  sorry
135	
136	/--
137	The universal property of the Jacobian variety: For any abelian variety `A`, any morphism
138	`f : C ⟶ A` with `f(P) = 0` factors uniquely through the Jacobian of `C`. In other words,
139	`Jacobian C` is the Albanese variety of `C`.
140	-/
141	theorem exists_unique_ofCurve_comp (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
142	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
143	    (P : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ C)
144	    {A : Over (Spec (.of k))} [Smooth A.hom] [IsProper A.hom] [GrpObj A]
145	    [GeometricallyIrreducible A.hom] (f : C ⟶ A) (hf : P ≫ f = η[A]) :
146	    ∃! (g : Jacobian C ⟶ A), f = ofCurve P ≫ g :=
147	  sorry
148	
149	/-- **Functoriality of the Jacobian**, bundled as a single contravariant functor: a curve goes to
150	its Jacobian group scheme over `k`, and a morphism of curves to the pullback of line bundles. The
151	functor laws (`map_id`, `map_comp`) are embedded in this `Functor`. The object action is pinned to
152	the `Jacobian` above, so everything downstream stays phrased in terms of `Jacobian C`. -/
153	noncomputable def functor (k : Type u) [Field k] :
154	    (Curve k)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Grp (Over (Spec (.of k))) where
155	  obj X := .mk (Jacobian X.unop.carrier)
156	  map _ := sorry
157	  map_id := sorry
158	  map_comp := sorry
159	
160	end Jacobian
161	
162	/-! ## Base change of fields
163	
164	Base change of `k`-schemes along `k → L` sends `X` to `X ×_{Spec k} Spec L`. These definitions and
165	the stability instances are genuine (no `sorry`); they set up the statements of the base-change
166	compatibility of the Jacobian. -/
167	
168	/-- Base change of `k`-schemes along a field homomorphism `k → L`, i.e. `X ↦ X ×_{Spec k} Spec L`.
169	-/
170	noncomputable abbrev baseChange (k L : Type u) [Field k] [Field L] [Algebra k L] :
171	    Over (Spec (.of k)) ⥤ Over (Spec (.of L)) :=
172	  Over.pullback (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k L)))
173	
174	instance {k L : Type u} [Field k] [Field L] [Algebra k L] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
175	    [IsProper C.hom] : IsProper ((baseChange k L).obj C).hom :=
176	  MorphismProperty.baseChange_obj (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k L))) C inferInstance
177	
178	instance {k L : Type u} [Field k] [Field L] [Algebra k L] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
179	    [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] : GeometricallyIrreducible ((baseChange k L).obj C).hom :=
180	  MorphismProperty.baseChange_obj (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k L))) C inferInstance
181	
182	instance {k L : Type u} [Field k] [Field L] [Algebra k L] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
183	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] :
184	    SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 ((baseChange k L).obj C).hom :=
185	  have : MorphismProperty.IsStableUnderBaseChange (@SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1) :=
186	    smoothOfRelativeDimension_isStableUnderBaseChange 1
187	  MorphismProperty.baseChange_obj (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k L))) C inferInstance
188	
189	-- The coherences mention curves of the form `(𝟭 _).obj C` and `(F ⋙ G).obj C`.
190	instance {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom] :
191	    IsProper ((𝟭 (Over (Spec (.of k)))).obj C).hom := ‹_›
192	instance {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
193	    GeometricallyIrreducible ((𝟭 (Over (Spec (.of k)))).obj C).hom := ‹_›
194	instance {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] :
195	    SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 ((𝟭 (Over (Spec (.of k)))).obj C).hom := ‹_›
196	
197	instance {k L M : Type u} [Field k] [Field L] [Field M] [Algebra k L] [Algebra L M]
198	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom] :
199	    IsProper ((baseChange k L ⋙ baseChange L M).obj C).hom :=
200	  inferInstanceAs (IsProper ((baseChange L M).obj ((baseChange k L).obj C)).hom)
201	instance {k L M : Type u} [Field k] [Field L] [Field M] [Algebra k L] [Algebra L M]
202	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
203	    GeometricallyIrreducible ((baseChange k L ⋙ baseChange L M).obj C).hom :=
204	  inferInstanceAs (GeometricallyIrreducible ((baseChange L M).obj ((baseChange k L).obj C)).hom)
205	instance {k L M : Type u} [Field k] [Field L] [Field M] [Algebra k L] [Algebra L M]
206	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] :
207	    SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 ((baseChange k L ⋙ baseChange L M).obj C).hom :=
208	  inferInstanceAs (SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 ((baseChange L M).obj ((baseChange k L).obj C)).hom)
209	
210	/-- Base change along `k → k` is the identity functor. -/
211	noncomputable def baseChange.idIso (k : Type u) [Field k] :
212	    baseChange k k ≅ 𝟭 (Over (Spec (.of k))) :=
213	  eqToIso (by
214	    change Over.pullback (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k k))) = Over.pullback (𝟙 _)
215	    rw [Algebra.algebraMap_self, CommRingCat.ofHom_id, Spec.map_id]) ≪≫ Over.pullbackId
216	
217	/-- Base change along a tower `k → L → M` is the composite of the two base changes. -/
218	noncomputable def baseChange.compIso (k L M : Type u) [Field k] [Field L] [Field M]
219	    [Algebra k L] [Algebra L M] [Algebra k M] [IsScalarTower k L M] :
220	    baseChange k M ≅ baseChange k L ⋙ baseChange L M :=
221	  eqToIso (by
222	    change Over.pullback (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k M))) =
223	      Over.pullback (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap L M)) ≫
224	        Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k L)))
225	    rw [← Spec.map_comp, ← CommRingCat.ofHom_comp, ← IsScalarTower.algebraMap_eq]) ≪≫
226	    Over.pullbackComp _ _
227	
228	namespace Jacobian
229	
230	/-- The Jacobian respects isomorphisms of curves — *derived* from the bundled functor
231	`Jacobian.functor` via `Functor.mapIso`, not a primitive. Used to compare the two sides of the
232	cocycle, whose curves agree only up to `baseChange.compIso`. -/
233	noncomputable def congr {k : Type u} [Field k] {C C' : Over (Spec (.of k))}
234	    [IsProper C.hom] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
235	    [IsProper C'.hom] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C'.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C'.hom]
236	    (e : C ≅ C') :
237	    (.mk (Jacobian C) : Grp (Over (Spec (.of k)))) ≅ .mk (Jacobian C') :=
238	  let j : (⟨C⟩ : Curve k) ≅ ⟨C'⟩ :=
239	    { hom := e.hom, inv := e.inv, hom_inv_id := e.hom_inv_id, inv_hom_id := e.inv_hom_id }
240	  (Jacobian.functor k).mapIso j.symm.op
241	
242	/-- **The base-change condition.** Jacobians commute with base change of fields: a canonical
243	isomorphism `Jac(C)_L ≅ Jac(C_L)`, as group schemes over `L`. -/
244	noncomputable def baseChangeIso (k L : Type u) [Field k] [Field L] [Algebra k L]
245	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
246	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
247	    (baseChange k L).mapGrp.obj (.mk (Jacobian C)) ≅ .mk (Jacobian ((baseChange k L).obj C)) :=
248	  sorry
249	
250	/-! ## Functoriality: the base change isomorphisms form a coherent system. -/
251	
252	/-- Identity coherence. -/
253	theorem baseChangeIso_id (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
254	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
255	    baseChangeIso k k C =
256	      (Functor.mapGrpNatIso (baseChange.idIso k)).app _
257	        ≪≫ (Functor.mapGrpIdIso (C := Over (Spec (.of k)))).app _
258	        ≪≫ Jacobian.congr ((baseChange.idIso k).app C).symm :=
259	  sorry
260	
261	/-- Cocycle coherence for a tower `k → L → M`. -/
262	theorem baseChangeIso_comp (k L M : Type u) [Field k] [Field L] [Field M]
263	    [Algebra k L] [Algebra L M] [Algebra k M] [IsScalarTower k L M]
264	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
265	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
266	    baseChangeIso k M C
267	        ≪≫ Jacobian.congr ((baseChange.compIso k L M).app C) =
268	      (Functor.mapGrpNatIso (baseChange.compIso k L M)).app _
269	        ≪≫ (Functor.mapGrpCompIso (F := baseChange k L) (G := baseChange L M)).app _
270	        ≪≫ (baseChange L M).mapGrp.mapIso (baseChangeIso k L C)
271	        ≪≫ baseChangeIso L M ((baseChange k L).obj C) :=
272	  sorry
273	
274	/-! ## Compatibility with the Abel-Jacobi map -/
275	
276	variable {L : Type u} [Field L] [Algebra k L]
277	
278	theorem baseChange_ofCurve (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
279	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
280	    (P : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ C) :
281	    (baseChange k L).map (ofCurve P) ≫ (baseChangeIso k L C).hom.hom.hom =
282	      ofCurve (Functor.LaxMonoidal.ε (baseChange k L) ≫ (baseChange k L).map P) :=
283	  sorry
284	
285	end Jacobian
286	
287	end AlgebraicGeometry

# Route decision — the mathematical architecture of the rebuild

*2026-07-11, Fable-5 design session. Inputs: a 5-agent survey (mathlib v4.31.0 capability
inventory; old-draft map; Kleiman/FGA route DAG; alternative-routes survey; operational
lessons). Survey reports are archived in the session scratchpad; their load-bearing
conclusions are restated here so this document is self-contained.*

This document fixes the route for all 14 protected targets in
`AlgebraicJacobian/Challenge.lean` and the design rules every wave must follow.
It is the map; the blueprint is the mathematics; the Lean tree is the proof.

## 1. The route in one paragraph

**`Jacobian C := Pic⁰_{C/k}`**, the identity component of the scheme representing the
étale-sheafified relative Picard functor of `C/k` (Kleiman, *The Picard Scheme*, FGA
Explained ch. 5). Representability is the central mountain (Grothendieck's Thm 4.8,
specialized hard to a smooth proper geometrically irreducible curve over a field).
The Albanese universal property is proved Milne-style (*Abelian Varieties* III.6.1):
symmetric powers `C^(g) → J` birational, rational maps into abelian varieties extend
(Milne I.3.2 = I.3.1 + Lemma 3.3), rigidity makes the factorization a homomorphism,
uniqueness descends from `k̄` to `k`. The genus is `g(C) := dim_k H¹(C, 𝒪_C)` with
`H¹` the derived-functor cohomology of the Zariski site of `C` valued in `ModuleCat k`,
computed by a pinned 2-affine-cover Mayer–Vietoris cokernel and proved finite by the
two-lattice ladder over a finite map `C → ℙ¹`. Every functorial target (`functor`,
`baseChangeIso`, the coherences) is a uniqueness-of-representing-object corollary of a
single pinned `RepresentableBy` datum — never a `Classical.choice` extraction.

Why not the alternatives (survey verdicts):

- **Weil group-chunk construction (Sym^g + birational group law): rejected.** Its
  obligations (scheme quotients by finite groups, relative divisors,
  cohomology-and-base-change, Weil's globalization theorem, plus a descent problem for
  pointless curves — the challenge's `Jacobian` takes **no rational point**) meet or
  exceed the FGA debt, and the functorial targets would still have to be re-derived
  through the Pic functor afterwards (Milne III.7.6). FGA's Thm 4.8 needs no point;
  that is a structural advantage for this exact statement file.
- **Kleiman's own Albanese derivation (`rmk:Alb`): rejected** — it outsources dual
  abelian varieties, autoduality (`Ĵ ≅ J`, [EGK Thm 2.1], unproved in our references)
  and projectivity of abelian varieties. Milne III.6.1 is strictly lighter and its
  ingredients (Sym^g, Riemann–Roch) are shared with the `Div^d`-representability leg,
  so their cost is amortized.

## 2. Ground truth about mathlib v4.31.0 (verified in the checkout, not from memory)

**Gifts to design around** (all present):

- Group objects: `GrpObj`, bundled `Grp C`, `Functor.mapGrp/mapGrpIdIso/mapGrpCompIso/
  mapGrpNatIso` — the challenge's vocabulary, complete. **`GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy`**:
  a representing object of a group-valued functor gets `GrpObj` for free.
- `AlgebraicGeometry/Group/Abelian.lean`: `isCommMonObj_of_isProper_of_geometricallyIntegral`
  (proper geometrically integral group scheme over a field is commutative) — the
  rigidity *corollary* is already a theorem.
- `AlgebraicGeometry/Group/Smooth.lean`: `smooth_of_grpObj` (geometrically reduced +
  locally finite type group scheme over a field ⇒ smooth) — kills the deformation-theory
  half of smoothness; what remains of `smoothOfRelativeDimension_genus` is
  `T₀J ≅ H¹(C,𝒪_C)` plus dimension bookkeeping.
- `Sites/Representability.lean` (Zariski sheaf glued from representable opens is
  representable, Stacks 01JJ), `subcanonical_zariskiTopology`, the étale/fppf/fpqc sites.
- `ZariskisMainTheorem.lean`: `IsFinite.of_isProper_of_locallyQuasiFinite` — the
  finite-map-to-ℙ¹ leg shrinks.
- Sheaf cohomology `Sheaf.H` via `Ext` + Grothendieck-abelian `HasExt`/`EnoughInjectives`
  + the Mayer–Vietoris LES (`Sites/SheafCohomology/`) — at `AddCommGrpCat`; the
  `ModuleCat k` twin is ours to build (de-risked: the old draft did it).
- `IsProper`/`SmoothOfRelativeDimension`/`Geometrically*` with exactly the stability
  instances the frozen file consumes; valuative criterion over arbitrary valuation rings;
  `Proj` + its properness; function fields; Dedekind/`HeightOneSpectrum` valuation stack;
  `RingTheory/Invariant` (`A^G`); rational maps (`Birational/RationalMap.lean` — no
  extension theorems though).

**Load-bearing absences** (each is ours to build; nothing above Layer A of the DAG exists):
coherent cohomology of schemes (any `H^i(X,F)`, `R^i f_*`, base change, finiteness,
vanishing); line bundles / `Pic` of a scheme; Weil/Cartier divisors, degrees, `L(D)`;
Riemann–Roch / Serre duality in any form; ampleness / projectivity vocabulary / `𝒪(d)` /
Serre finiteness; Hilbert/Quot/Grassmannian schemes; quotients of schemes (finite groups
or equivalence relations); symmetric powers; relative effective divisors; rigidity;
rational-map extension theorems; smooth ⇒ geometrically reduced; Auslander–Buchsbaum;
DVR refinement of the valuative criterion; genus (zero hits in all of Mathlib).

## 3. Definitions of record (the semantic pins)

- **genus**: `genus C := Module.finrank k (H¹ₖ(C, 𝒪_C))` where `Hⁿₖ(C, F)` is the
  Ext-based cohomology of the (essentially small) Zariski site of `C` with values in
  `ModuleCat k`, applied to the structure sheaf viewed as a sheaf of `k`-modules.
  *Not* a Čech-carrier definition: the derived definition is canonical
  (cover-independent by construction), mathlib-idiomatic, and the MV (0,1)-slice
  gives the 2-cover cokernel computation as a theorem, gate-free (old draft proved
  this bridge end to end; we re-derive it).
- **Jacobian**: the representing object of the degree-0 part of the étale-sheafified
  relative Picard functor, carried as a **pinned `RepresentableBy` datum** (data, not
  `Nonempty`), from which `instGrpObj` is `GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy`, `functor.map` is
  precomposition of represented functors, and `baseChangeIso` + coherences are
  uniqueness-of-representing-object arguments.
- **ofCurve**: the Abel–Jacobi map `t ↦ [𝒪(Γ_t − P_T)]` via graph divisors
  (`Div¹_{C/k} = C`), landing in `Pic⁰` because `C` is connected and `P ↦ 0`.
- **Albanese UP**: Milne III.6.1 over `k̄`, descended to `k` uniqueness-first
  (Milne 6.4-pattern). Note the challenge asks uniqueness among **plain** `Over`-morphisms;
  rigidity converts any competitor into a homomorphism (it is pointed:
  `η ≫ g = P ≫ ofCurve P ≫ g = P ≫ f = η`), and homomorphisms agreeing on the
  generating curve agree.

## 4. Proof-obligation DAG (cost-ordered waves)

Difficulty: [R] routine, [S] substantial, [RG] research-grade-for-mathlib.
The four [RG] clusters are: representability (B4), Albanese (N12), properness (N5),
and the coherent-cohomology substrate they stand on. Everything else is [R]/[S] given
its predecessors.

### Wave 1 — curve substrate + the genus lane (fully de-risked; do first)
1. `Curve/Basic` [R–S]: standing consequences of the hypothesis bundle — integral,
   quasi-compact, separated; `Γ(C,𝒪_C) ≅ k` (via mathlib's
   `isIso_pushoutSection_of_isQuasiSeparated_of_flat_right` + properness `isField`
   facts); function field; stalk dimension ≤ 1 on standard-smooth rel-dim-1 charts.
2. `Curve/GeometricallyReduced` [S]: **smooth ⇒ geometrically reduced** (fibers of a
   smooth morphism are geometrically regular). Mathlib gap under EVERY target: the
   frozen file says `GeometricallyIrreducible`; all the real mathematics needs
   `GeometricallyIntegral`. Settled here once, as an instance.
3. `Cohomology/*` [S]: `ModuleCat k`-valued sheaf cohomology `Hⁿₖ` (Grothendieck-abelian
   ⇒ `HasExt`, universe discipline fixed once); degree-1 vanishing on affines;
   2-affine-cover MV square + `H1Cok` cokernel carrier; the MV (0,1)-slice bridge
   `H¹ₖ(C,𝒪) ≃ₗ[k] H1Cok`.

# Wave-3 design spec — the Picard-functor lane

*2026-07-11, Fable-5 Wave-3 design session. **Binding** for route-decision §4 items 8–10 and for
the interfaces Waves 4/5/7 consume. Inputs, all read in full or in the cited sections:
`informal/route-decision.md`, `informal/wave3-mathlib-survey.md`,
`informal/old-draft-picard-recon.md`, `AlgebraicJacobian/Challenge.lean` (frozen),
`AlgebraicJacobian/Cohomology/TwoCover.lean` (landed API), and Kleiman, *The Picard Scheme*
(`references/kleiman-picard-src/kleiman-picard.tex`, TeX source; reading log in §11).
Numbering of Kleiman items is reconstructed by counting numbered environments per section and
cross-checked against the known anchors (2.5 = `th:cmp`, 4.8 = `th:main`, 4.18.3 = `cor:algsch`,
5.1 = `lem:agps`); every citation below also gives the TeX `\label` so it is checkable
independently of the count.*

Lean signatures below are **intended signatures**: binding in shape (carrier types, universes,
variance, what is data vs Prop), lane-owned in spelling (final names follow mathlib conventions;
defeq-level plumbing may adjust). Anything marked **OPEN-n** is an undecided sub-point with its
closing criterion in §9.

---

## 0. Decisions at a glance

| # | Decision | Section |
|---|----------|---------|
| D1 | Definitional Pic = Čech H¹ of the units presheaf on the small Zariski site: **pointed covers** (one open per point), built **on mathlib's `PresheafOfGroups.H1`** fixed-family layer, refinement colimit as a sigma-type quotient, everything in `Type u`. | §2 |
| D2 | Group structure **multiplicative**, `CommGroup` carriers, `CommGrpCat.{u}`-valued functors. | §2.4 |
| D3 | Relative functor = H_T-coset quotient `Pic((C ⊗ T).left) ⧸ range(snd-pullback)` on `(Over (Spec k))ᵒᵖ`, `CommGrpCat.{u}`-valued. Never the absolute `Pic(C×T)`. | §3 |
| D4 | Étale sheafification = **hand-rolled one-step plus** over *presented* affine étale covers, on **affine** test schemes; extended to all of `Over (Spec k)` by the canonical limit over affine opens (dense-subsite Kan extension). One plus suffices because `relPic` is étale-separated (Kleiman 2.5(1) recast; hypothesis discharged by `ex:gc&r`). Option (iii) "representability becomes the definition" is **rejected as a definition** and retained as the Wave-4 **proof strategy**; the functor `J` represents is construction-canonical. | §4 |
| D5 | `JacobianData C` = structure with fields `J`, the `RepresentableBy` **datum** for the degree-0 functor, and `LocallyOfFiniteType` + `QuasiCompact` certificates. Consumed as a section variable; discharged by a Wave-4 *def* `jacobianData C`, never `Nonempty` + choice, never a sorried instance. | §5 |
| D6 | Degree defined over fields via the divisor/χ ledger owned by Wave 2 (interface pinned here, B4 pushforward-rank shape as the normalization `deg 𝒪(D) = finrank`); `Pic⁰` = subfunctor of classes with degree 0 at **every field-valued point** of the test scheme. | §6 |
| D7 | `baseChangeIso` will consume degree-invariance under field extension (χ-ledger), **not** identity-component theory; `lem:agps`(3) remains needed only for `GeometricallyIrreducible`. Deviation from route Wave-7 item 20 wording, justified in §10. | §6.3, §10 |
| D8 | 12 new Lean files (§7), 5 immediately parallel lanes, keystone = the `GrpObj`-derivation dry-run compile against the frozen `instGrpObj` shape. | §7 |

---

## 1. Standing conventions

- **Universe discipline: everything at `u`.** `Scheme.{u}`, test category `Over (Spec (.of k))`
  with hom-types in `Type u`, all Pic carriers in `Type u`, all functors valued in
  `CommGrpCat.{u}`. This is forced by `GrpObj.ofRepresentableBy`
  (`Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Monoidal/Cartesian/Grp.lean:35`), which couples the universe of the
  representing object's homs with the functor's value universe (survey "Universe landmines").
  `JacobianData C` itself lives in `Type (u+1)` (it contains a scheme); that is harmless.
- **Hypothesis bundle.** Every file uses the frozen variable block
  `{k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom]
  [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]`, plus the Wave-1 derived instance
  `GeometricallyIntegral C.hom` (route Wave-1 item 2) whenever integrality is used.
- **Product language.** All products of test objects are the cartesian-monoidal product in
  `Over (Spec (.of k))` (`CategoryTheory/Monoidal/Cartesian/Over.lean:34`,
  `Over.cartesianMonoidalCategory`, chosen via `Limits.pullback`): `C ⊗ T`, projections
  `fst C T`, `snd C T`, whiskering `C ◁ g`. This is the vocabulary of the frozen file
  (`𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k)))`, `η[·]`, `Functor.LaxMonoidal.ε`). Descents to `Scheme`-level
  pullbacks (`(C ⊗ T).left`) happen only inside cocycle constructions, with the bridge lemmas
  confined to `Picard/RelFunctor.lean`. Known wall: `Over.pullback` instance opacity — use the
  route rule 9 fixes (point-level `congrArg` calc chains, `erw [Category.comp_id]`).
- **Verification bar** (route rule 7): `lake build <Module>` kernel check, then `lean_verify`
  axiom audit (`propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound` only) on each keystone. LSP advisory only.
- Category names verified in the v4.31 checkout: bundled concrete categories are `GrpCat`,
  `CommGrpCat`, `CommMonCat` (e.g. `CommMonCat.units : CommMonCat.{u} ⥤ CommGrpCat.{u}`,
  `Mathlib/Algebra/Category/Grp/Adjunctions.lean:202`); bundled group *objects* are
  `CategoryTheory.Grp C` (`Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Monoidal/Grp.lean:82`), the challenge's
  `Grp (Over (Spec (.of k)))`.

---

## 2. (A) The definitional Pic carrier

**Semantic pin.** For any scheme `X`, the Picard group *of record* is the Čech cohomology
`Ȟ¹(X, 𝒪_X^*)` on the small Zariski site: covers by opens, unit-valued 1-cocycles modulo
coboundaries, colimit over refinement. This is recon lesson 1 verbatim, and it is Kleiman's own
remark `rk:coh` (§2.11): "for any ringed space `R`, there is a natural isomorphism
`Pic(R) = H¹(R, 𝒪_R^*)`" (his eq. 2.11.2 = `eq:2b`, citing Hartshorne III Ex. 4.5).

**Semantic-honesty remark (record in the blueprint chapter).** The frozen `Challenge.lean` never
mentions `Pic`, line bundles, or invertible sheaves; the only consumers of the carrier are the
functors and elements defined in this spec. Therefore the comparison
"`CechPic X ≃ {invertible 𝒪_X-modules}/≅`" is **Phase-2 optional** (a `ForMathlib` PR
candidate), and no Wave depends on it. What is **Phase-1 mandatory** is that `𝒪(D)`-classes of
relative effective divisors be constructible as explicit cocycles from local equations, because
`ofCurve` is pinned as `t ↦ [𝒪(Γ_t − P_T)]` (route §3). §2.6 pins that constructor.

### 2.1 Index discipline: pointed covers, arbitrary opens

```lean
/-- A pointed open cover of a scheme: one open per point, containing it. -/
structure Scheme.PointedCover (X : Scheme.{u}) : Type u where
  opens : X → X.Opens
  mem_opens : ∀ x, x ∈ opens x
```

with the refinement preorder `𝒱 ≤ 𝒰 ↔ ∀ x, 𝒱.opens x ≤ 𝒰.opens x`.

Decision rationale (each alternative was weighed):

- **Not finite covers, not affine covers, not `Set X.Opens`.** Pointed covers give:
  (a) *smallness for free* — the index type is the fixed carrier `X : Type u`, so the sigma type
  in §2.3 stays in `Type u`; (b) *canonical refinement maps* — a refinement `𝒱 ≤ 𝒰` refines
  **indexwise** (`𝒱.opens x ≤ 𝒰.opens x`), so the cocycle-restriction map needs no choice of a
  reindexing function and no "independence of the refinement map" lemma at the carrier level;
  (c) *directedness by pointwise `⊓`* (`(𝒰 ⊓ 𝒱).opens x := 𝒰.opens x ⊓ 𝒱.opens x`), so the
  refinement colimit is filtered; (d) *clean pullback* — for `f : X ⟶ Y` the pulled-back cover is
  `x ↦ f ⁻¹ᵁ (𝒰.opens (f x))`, again pointed, again indexed by the carrier. Affineness
  constraints would break (d) (preimages of affines are not affine); `Set`-indexing breaks (b)
  (pullback collapses indices).
- Affine or finite covers re-enter as *cofinality lemmas*, not as carrier structure: every
  pointed cover is refined by a pointed affine cover (`x ↦` an affine open neighbourhood inside
  `𝒰.opens x`; the choice lives inside a `Prop`, so no data escapes). This is where the
  2-cover computations of the χ-ledger and the T₀ engine plug in.

### 2.2 The cocycle layer: build on `PresheafOfGroups.H1`

**Decision: build on mathlib's fixed-family layer**, not hand-rolled. Instantiation:

```lean
/-- The units presheaf of a scheme, on its small Zariski site. -/
def Scheme.unitsPresheaf (X : Scheme.{u}) : (X.Opens)ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat.{u} :=
  X.presheaf ⋙ forget₂ CommRingCat CommMonCat ⋙ CommMonCat.units
-- (OPEN-4: if the `forget₂ CommRingCat CommMonCat` path is absent in v4.31, a ~20-line
-- bespoke functor replaces the composition; the statement shape is unchanged.)

abbrev Scheme.unitsCocycle (X : Scheme.{u}) (𝒰 : X.PointedCover) :=
  PresheafOfGroups.OneCocycle (X.unitsPresheaf ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) 𝒰.opens
```

Here the site category is the poset `X.Opens`, the family is `𝒰.opens : X → X.Opens`, and
mathlib's `OneCochain/OneCocycle/OneCohomologyRelation/IsCohomologous/H1` + `One (H1 G U)`
(`Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Sites/NonabelianCohomology/H1.lean:58–197`) come for free. On a poset
with infima, the `ev (i j) (a : T ⟶ U i) (b : T ⟶ U j)`-style cochain is *equivalent* to the
classical pair data `g x y ∈ 𝒪ˣ(𝒰x ⊓ 𝒰y)` with the cocycle condition on triple infima: homs
are subsingletons, so `ev` is determined by its value at `T = 𝒰x ⊓ 𝒰y` via `ev_precomp`, and
`ev_trans` at the triple infimum is the classical condition. **Binding ergonomic requirement**:
`Picard/CechH1.lean` must provide the two-way bridge so lane agents never touch `ev` directly:

```lean
/-- Build a 1-cocycle over a poset with binary infima from classical pair data. -/
def PresheafOfGroups.OneCocycle.ofPairs
    (g : ∀ x y, G.obj (op (𝒰.opens x ⊓ 𝒰.opens y)))
    (hg : ∀ x y z, /- restrictions to the triple infimum satisfy g x y · g y z = g x z -/) :
    OneCocycle G 𝒰.opens
lemma ev_inf (γ : OneCocycle G 𝒰.opens) (x y) : γ.ev x y ⋯ = ⋯   -- extraction at the infimum
```

Additions ours to make (all in `Picard/CechH1.lean`, stated generically over any `Cᵒᵖ ⥤
CommGrpCat.{w}` — a mathlib-PR candidate, their file's TODO list asks for exactly this):

- `Mul/Inv/CommGroup (OneCocycle Gc U)` when the presheaf is commutative-group-valued (the
  product of cocycles satisfies `ev_trans` only using commutativity), and the descended
  `CommGroup (H1 Gc U)` via `Quot.map₂` (compatibility of `IsCohomologous` with products again
  uses commutativity).
- Restriction along an indexwise refinement `res : H1 G 𝒰 →* H1 G 𝒱` for `𝒱 ≤ 𝒰`

12	sheaf on the small Zariski site (the poset `X.Opens`), valued in `CommGrpCat`, together
13	with the element-level interface used by the Čech `H¹` layer of the Picard group:
14

16	* pullback of a unit section along a morphism of schemes, packaged as
17	  `Scheme.Hom.unitsAppLE` (the unit-group analogue of `Scheme.Hom.appLE`), with the same
18	  composition/restriction calculus as `appLE`.

23	  `X.presheaf ⋙ forget₂ CommRingCat CommMonCat ⋙ CommMonCat.units`, a functor
24	  `(X.Opens)ᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat.{u}`.

28	  `U ≤ f ⁻¹ᵁ V`, the group homomorphism `Γ(Y, V)ˣ →* Γ(X, U)ˣ`.
29	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Hom.unitsAppLE_map`, `Scheme.Hom.map_unitsAppLE`,
30	  `Scheme.Hom.unitsAppLE_unitsAppLE`, `Scheme.id_unitsAppLE`: the calculus mirroring
31	  `appLE_map`, `map_appLE`, `appLE_comp_appLE` and `id_app` at the unit level.

49	  X.presheaf ⋙ forget₂ CommRingCat CommMonCat ⋙ CommMonCat.units

325	  refine ⟨fun x y ↦ ?_⟩
326	  induction x using Quot.ind with
327	  | _ γ =>
328	    induction y using Quot.ind with
329	    | _ δ =>
330	      exact Quot.sound ((OneCocycle.equivalence_isCohomologous G U).trans
331	        ((OneCocycle.equivalence_isCohomologous G U).symm (key γ)) (key δ))
332	
333	end Poset

335	/-! ## Commutative values: the group structure on cocycles and `H1` -/
336	
337	section Comm
338	
339	variable {G : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ CommGrpCat.{w}} {U V : I → C}
340	
341	private lemma val_mul_comm {X : Cᵒᵖ}
342	    (x y : ((G ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat).obj X)) : x * y = y * x := by
343	  letI : CommGroup ((G ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat).obj X) := (G.obj X).str
344	  exact mul_comm x y
345	
346	private lemma val_mul_mul_mul_comm {X : Cᵒᵖ}
347	    (a b c d : ((G ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat).obj X)) :
348	    a * b * (c * d) = a * c * (b * d) := by
349	  letI : CommGroup ((G ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat).obj X) := (G.obj X).str
350	  exact mul_mul_mul_comm a b c d
351	
352	namespace OneCocycle
353	
354	/-- The product of two 1-cocycles valued in commutative groups (the cocycle condition
355	for the product cochain uses commutativity). -/
356	protected def mul (γ₁ γ₂ : OneCocycle (G ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) U) :
357	    OneCocycle (G ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) U where
358	  toOneCochain := γ₁.toOneCochain * γ₂.toOneCochain
359	  ev_trans i j k T a b c := by
360	    simp only [OneCochain.mul_ev]
361	    rw [val_mul_mul_mul_comm, γ₁.ev_trans i j k a b c, γ₂.ev_trans i j k a b c]
362	
363	/-- The inverse of a 1-cocycle valued in commutative groups. -/
364	protected def inv (γ : OneCocycle (G ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) U) :
365	    OneCocycle (G ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) U where
366	  toOneCochain := γ.toOneCochain⁻¹
367	  ev_trans i j k T a b c := by
368	    simp only [OneCochain.inv_ev]
369	    rw [← mul_inv_rev, val_mul_comm, γ.ev_trans i j k a b c]
370	
371	instance : CommGroup (OneCocycle (G ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) U) where
372	  mul := OneCocycle.mul
373	  one := 1
374	  inv := OneCocycle.inv
375	  mul_assoc a b c := toOneCochain_injective (mul_assoc _ _ _)
376	  one_mul a := toOneCochain_injective (one_mul _)
377	  mul_one a := toOneCochain_injective (mul_one _)
378	  inv_mul_cancel a := toOneCochain_injective (inv_mul_cancel _)
379	  mul_comm a b := toOneCochain_injective (by ext i j T x y; exact val_mul_comm _ _)
380	
381	@[simp]
382	lemma mul_toOneCochain (γ₁ γ₂ : OneCocycle (G ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) U) :
383	    (γ₁ * γ₂).toOneCochain = γ₁.toOneCochain * γ₂.toOneCochain :=
384	  rfl
385	
386	@[simp]
387	lemma inv_toOneCochain (γ : OneCocycle (G ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) U) :
388	    (γ⁻¹).toOneCochain = γ.toOneCochain⁻¹ :=
389	  rfl
390	
391	@[simp]
392	lemma mul_res (γ₁ γ₂ : OneCocycle (G ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) U)
393	    (f : ∀ i, V i ⟶ U i) : (γ₁ * γ₂).res f = γ₁.res f * γ₂.res f :=
394	  rfl
395	
396	@[simp]
397	lemma inv_res (γ : OneCocycle (G ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) U)
398	    (f : ∀ i, V i ⟶ U i) : (γ⁻¹).res f = (γ.res f)⁻¹ :=
399	  rfl
400	
401	end OneCocycle
402	
403	lemma OneCohomologyRelation.mul
404	    {γ₁ γ₂ δ₁ δ₂ : OneCochain (G ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) U}
405	    {α β : ZeroCochain (G ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) U}
406	    (h : OneCohomologyRelation γ₁ γ₂ α) (h' : OneCohomologyRelation δ₁ δ₂ β) :
407	    OneCohomologyRelation (γ₁ * δ₁) (γ₂ * δ₂) (α * β) := by
408	  intro i j T a b
409	  simp only [OneCochain.mul_ev, Cochain₀.mul_apply, map_mul]
410	  rw [val_mul_mul_mul_comm _ _ (γ₁.ev i j a b), h i j a b, h' i j a b,
411	    val_mul_mul_mul_comm (γ₂.ev i j a b)]
412	
413	lemma OneCohomologyRelation.inv {γ₁ γ₂ : OneCochain (G ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) U}
414	    {α : ZeroCochain (G ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) U}
415	    (h : OneCohomologyRelation γ₁ γ₂ α) :
416	    OneCohomologyRelation γ₁⁻¹ γ₂⁻¹ α⁻¹ := by
417	  intro i j T a b
418	  simp only [OneCochain.inv_ev, Cochain₀.inv_apply, map_inv]
419	  rw [← mul_inv_rev, ← mul_inv_rev,
420	    val_mul_comm (γ₁.ev i j a b) ((G ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat).map a.op (α i)),
421	    h i j a b,
422	    val_mul_comm (γ₂.ev i j a b) ((G ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat).map b.op (α j))]
423	
424	namespace OneCocycle
425	
426	lemma IsCohomologous.mul {γ₁ γ₂ δ₁ δ₂ : OneCocycle (G ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) U}
427	    (h : γ₁.IsCohomologous γ₂) (h' : δ₁.IsCohomologous δ₂) :
428	    (γ₁ * δ₁).IsCohomologous (γ₂ * δ₂) := by
429	  obtain ⟨α, hα⟩ := h
430	  obtain ⟨β, hβ⟩ := h'
431	  exact ⟨α * β, hα.mul hβ⟩
432	
433	lemma IsCohomologous.inv {γ₁ γ₂ : OneCocycle (G ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) U}
434	    (h : γ₁.IsCohomologous γ₂) : (γ₁⁻¹).IsCohomologous (γ₂⁻¹) := by
435	  obtain ⟨α, hα⟩ := h
436	  exact ⟨α⁻¹, hα.inv⟩
437	
438	protected lemma isCohomologous_refl (γ : OneCocycle (G ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) U) :
439	    γ.IsCohomologous γ :=
440	  (equivalence_isCohomologous _ _).refl γ
441	
442	end OneCocycle
443	
444	instance : CommGroup (H1 (G ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) U) where
445	  mul := Quot.map₂ (· * ·) (fun γ _ _ h ↦ γ.isCohomologous_refl.mul h)
446	    (fun _ _ δ h ↦ h.mul δ.isCohomologous_refl)
447	  one := 1
448	  inv := Quot.map (·⁻¹) (fun _ _ h ↦ h.inv)
449	  mul_assoc a b c := by
450	    obtain ⟨γ₁⟩ := a; obtain ⟨γ₂⟩ := b; obtain ⟨γ₃⟩ := c
451	    exact congrArg (Quot.mk _) (mul_assoc γ₁ γ₂ γ₃)
452	  one_mul a := by
453	    obtain ⟨γ⟩ := a
454	    exact congrArg (Quot.mk _) (one_mul γ)
455	  mul_one a := by
456	    obtain ⟨γ⟩ := a
457	    exact congrArg (Quot.mk _) (mul_one γ)
458	  inv_mul_cancel a := by
459	    obtain ⟨γ⟩ := a
460	    exact congrArg (Quot.mk _) (inv_mul_cancel γ)
461	  mul_comm a b := by
462	    obtain ⟨γ₁⟩ := a; obtain ⟨γ₂⟩ := b
463	    exact congrArg (Quot.mk _) (mul_comm γ₁ γ₂)
464	
465	namespace OneCocycle
466	
467	@[simp]
468	lemma class_one : (1 : OneCocycle (G ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) U).class = 1 :=
469	  rfl
470	
471	@[simp]
472	lemma class_mul (γ₁ γ₂ : OneCocycle (G ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) U) :
473	    (γ₁ * γ₂).class = γ₁.class * γ₂.class :=
474	  rfl
475	
476	@[simp]
477	lemma class_inv (γ : OneCocycle (G ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) U) :
478	    (γ⁻¹).class = γ.class⁻¹ :=
479	  rfl
480	
481	end OneCocycle

483	/-- Restriction of `H1` classes along an indexwise refinement, as a group homomorphism
484	(for presheaves of commutative groups). -/
485	def H1.resHom (f : ∀ i, V i ⟶ U i) :
486	    H1 (G ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) U →* H1 (G ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) V where
487	  toFun := H1.res f
488	  map_one' := rfl
489	  map_mul' x y := by
490	    obtain ⟨γ₁⟩ := x; obtain ⟨γ₂⟩ := y
491	    exact congrArg (Quot.mk _) (γ₁.mul_res γ₂ f)
492	
493	@[simp]
494	lemma H1.resHom_apply (f : ∀ i, V i ⟶ U i) (x : H1 (G ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) U) :
495	    H1.resHom f x = H1.res f x :=
496	  rfl

7	/-!
8	# The definitional Picard group: Čech `H¹` of the units presheaf
9	
10	For a scheme `X`, this file defines the Picard group of record of this development:
11	the Čech cohomology `Ȟ¹(X, 𝒪_X^*)` on the small Zariski site, computed on **pointed
12	covers** (one open per point of `X`) and stabilized along the refinement preorder.
13	Pointed covers keep everything in `Type u` (the index type is the carrier of `X`),
14	refine indexwise (no reindexing functions), and are directed by pointwise `⊓`.
15	
16	## Main declarations
17	
18	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.PointedCover`: one open per point, containing it; a
19	  `SemilatticeInf` with an `OrderTop`, refinement `𝒱 ≤ 𝒰 ↔ ∀ x, 𝒱.opens x ≤ 𝒰.opens x`.
20	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.unitsCocycle`, `Scheme.unitsH1`: unit-valued Čech 1-cocycles
21	  and `H¹` on a pointed cover; `Scheme.unitsRes`: restriction along a refinement,
22	  a group homomorphism, strictly functorial (`unitsRes_unitsRes`).
23	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.CechPic`: the Picard group `Ȟ¹(X, 𝒪_X^*)` as the quotient
24	  of `Σ 𝒰, X.unitsH1 𝒰` by agreement on a common refinement, with its `CommGroup`
25	  structure and the constructor/eliminator API `CechPic.mk`, `CechPic.ind`,
26	  `CechPic.mk_eq_mk_iff`, `CechPic.mk_unitsRes`.
27	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.CechPic.map`: contravariant functoriality — for
28	  `f : X ⟶ Y` the pullback `Y.CechPic →* X.CechPic` — with the strict functor laws
29	  `CechPic.map_id` and `CechPic.map_comp` (the lane keystone).
30	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.CechPic.subsingleton_of_subsingleton`: on a scheme with a
31	  subsingleton underlying space (e.g. `Spec` of a field) the Picard group is trivial.
32	-/
33	
34	set_option autoImplicit false
35	
36	universe u
37	
38	open CategoryTheory Opposite CategoryTheory.PresheafOfGroups
39	
40	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
41	
42	namespace Scheme
43	
44	variable {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}}
45	
46	/-! ## Pointed covers -/
47	
48	/-- A pointed open cover of a scheme: one open per point, containing it. Pointed covers
49	are the index discipline of `Scheme.CechPic`: the index type is the carrier of `X` (so
50	everything stays in `Type u`), refinement is indexwise, and pointwise `⊓` makes the
51	refinement order directed. -/
52	structure PointedCover (X : Scheme.{u}) : Type u where
53	  /-- The member of the cover attached to a point. -/
54	  opens : X → X.Opens
55	  /-- Each point lies in its member. -/
56	  mem_opens : ∀ x, x ∈ opens x
57	
58	namespace PointedCover
59	
60	@[ext]
61	lemma ext {𝒰 𝒱 : X.PointedCover} (h : ∀ x, 𝒰.opens x = 𝒱.opens x) : 𝒰 = 𝒱 := by
62	  cases 𝒰; cases 𝒱
63	  simpa using funext h
64	
65	instance : SemilatticeInf X.PointedCover where
66	  le 𝒱 𝒰 := ∀ x, 𝒱.opens x ≤ 𝒰.opens x
67	  le_refl 𝒰 x := le_rfl
68	  le_trans 𝒰 𝒱 𝒲 h₁ h₂ x := (h₁ x).trans (h₂ x)
69	  le_antisymm 𝒰 𝒱 h₁ h₂ := ext fun x ↦ le_antisymm (h₁ x) (h₂ x)
70	  inf 𝒰 𝒱 :=
71	    { opens := fun x ↦ 𝒰.opens x ⊓ 𝒱.opens x
72	      mem_opens := fun x ↦ ⟨𝒰.mem_opens x, 𝒱.mem_opens x⟩ }
73	  inf_le_left 𝒰 𝒱 x := inf_le_left
74	  inf_le_right 𝒰 𝒱 x := inf_le_right
75	  le_inf 𝒰 𝒱 𝒲 h₁ h₂ x := le_inf (h₁ x) (h₂ x)
76	
77	instance : OrderTop X.PointedCover where
78	  top := { opens := fun _ ↦ ⊤, mem_opens := fun _ ↦ trivial }
79	  le_top 𝒰 x := le_top
80	
81	lemma le_def {𝒰 𝒱 : X.PointedCover} : 𝒱 ≤ 𝒰 ↔ ∀ x, 𝒱.opens x ≤ 𝒰.opens x :=
82	  Iff.rfl
83	
84	@[simp]
85	lemma inf_opens (𝒰 𝒱 : X.PointedCover) (x : X) :
86	    (𝒰 ⊓ 𝒱).opens x = 𝒰.opens x ⊓ 𝒱.opens x :=
87	  rfl
88	
89	@[simp]
90	lemma top_opens (x : X) : (⊤ : X.PointedCover).opens x = ⊤ :=
91	  rfl
92	
93	/-- The pullback of a pointed cover along a morphism of schemes: the pointed cover by
94	preimages, `x ↦ f ⁻¹ᵁ 𝒰.opens (f x)`. -/
95	def pullback (f : X ⟶ Y) (𝒰 : Y.PointedCover) : X.PointedCover where
96	  opens x := f ⁻¹ᵁ 𝒰.opens (f.base x)
97	  mem_opens x := 𝒰.mem_opens (f.base x)
98	
99	@[simp]
100	lemma pullback_opens (f : X ⟶ Y) (𝒰 : Y.PointedCover) (x : X) :
101	    (𝒰.pullback f).opens x = f ⁻¹ᵁ 𝒰.opens (f.base x) :=
102	  rfl
103	
104	lemma pullback_mono (f : X ⟶ Y) {𝒰 𝒱 : Y.PointedCover} (h : 𝒱 ≤ 𝒰) :
105	    𝒱.pullback f ≤ 𝒰.pullback f :=
106	  fun x ↦ ((TopologicalSpace.Opens.map f.base).map (homOfLE (h (f.base x)))).le
107	
108	end PointedCover
109	
110	/-! ## Unit cocycles on a pointed cover and their restriction -/
111	
112	/-- The unit-valued Čech 1-cocycles of `X` on a pointed cover. -/
113	abbrev unitsCocycle (X : Scheme.{u}) (𝒰 : X.PointedCover) : Type u :=
114	  PresheafOfGroups.OneCocycle (X.unitsPresheaf ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) 𝒰.opens
115	
116	/-- The unit-valued Čech `H¹` of `X` on a pointed cover. -/
117	abbrev unitsH1 (X : Scheme.{u}) (𝒰 : X.PointedCover) : Type u :=
118	  PresheafOfGroups.H1 (X.unitsPresheaf ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) 𝒰.opens
119	
120	/-- Restriction of unit Čech classes along a refinement of pointed covers, as a group
121	homomorphism. -/
122	def unitsRes {𝒰 𝒱 : X.PointedCover} (h : 𝒱 ≤ 𝒰) : X.unitsH1 𝒰 →* X.unitsH1 𝒱 :=
123	  H1.resHom fun x ↦ homOfLE (h x)
124	
125	/-- Restriction along refinements of pointed covers is strictly functorial. -/
126	@[simp]
127	lemma unitsRes_unitsRes {𝒰 𝒱 𝒲 : X.PointedCover} (h₁ : 𝒱 ≤ 𝒰) (h₂ : 𝒲 ≤ 𝒱)
128	    (a : X.unitsH1 𝒰) : unitsRes h₂ (unitsRes h₁ a) = unitsRes (h₂.trans h₁) a :=
129	  H1.res_res _ _ a
130	
131	@[simp]
132	lemma unitsRes_rfl {𝒰 : X.PointedCover} {h : 𝒰 ≤ 𝒰} (a : X.unitsH1 𝒰) :
133	    unitsRes h a = a :=
134	  H1.res_id a
135	
136	/-! ## The Picard group -/
137	
138	instance cechPicSetoid (X : Scheme.{u}) : Setoid (Σ 𝒰 : X.PointedCover, X.unitsH1 𝒰) where
139	  r p q := ∃ (𝒲 : X.PointedCover) (h₁ : 𝒲 ≤ p.1) (h₂ : 𝒲 ≤ q.1),
140	    unitsRes h₁ p.2 = unitsRes h₂ q.2
141	  iseqv := by
142	    constructor
143	    · exact fun p ↦ ⟨p.1, le_rfl, le_rfl, rfl⟩
144	    · rintro p q ⟨𝒲, h₁, h₂, e⟩
145	      exact ⟨𝒲, h₂, h₁, e.symm⟩
146	    · rintro p q r ⟨𝒲₁, h₁, h₂, e₁⟩ ⟨𝒲₂, h₃, h₄, e₂⟩
147	      refine ⟨𝒲₁ ⊓ 𝒲₂, inf_le_left.trans h₁, inf_le_right.trans h₄, ?_⟩
148	      have e₁' := congrArg (unitsRes (inf_le_left : 𝒲₁ ⊓ 𝒲₂ ≤ 𝒲₁)) e₁
149	      have e₂' := congrArg (unitsRes (inf_le_right : 𝒲₁ ⊓ 𝒲₂ ≤ 𝒲₂)) e₂
150	      simp only [unitsRes_unitsRes] at e₁' e₂'
151	      exact e₁'.trans e₂'
152	
153	/-- The definitional Picard group of a scheme: Čech `H¹` of the units presheaf,
154	stabilized along refinement of pointed covers. -/
155	def CechPic (X : Scheme.{u}) : Type u :=
156	  Quotient (cechPicSetoid X)
157	
158	namespace CechPic
159	
160	/-- The Picard class of a unit Čech `H¹` class on a pointed cover. -/
161	def mk (𝒰 : X.PointedCover) (a : X.unitsH1 𝒰) : X.CechPic :=
162	  ⟦⟨𝒰, a⟩⟧
163	
164	@[elab_as_elim]
165	theorem ind {motive : X.CechPic → Prop}
166	    (mk : ∀ (𝒰 : X.PointedCover) (a : X.unitsH1 𝒰), motive (mk 𝒰 a)) (x : X.CechPic) :
167	    motive x :=
168	  Quotient.ind (fun p ↦ by obtain ⟨𝒰, a⟩ := p; exact mk 𝒰 a) x
169	
170	theorem mk_eq_mk_iff {𝒰 𝒱 : X.PointedCover} {a : X.unitsH1 𝒰} {b : X.unitsH1 𝒱} :
171	    mk 𝒰 a = mk 𝒱 b ↔
172	      ∃ (𝒲 : X.PointedCover) (h₁ : 𝒲 ≤ 𝒰) (h₂ : 𝒲 ≤ 𝒱),
173	        unitsRes h₁ a = unitsRes h₂ b :=
174	  Quotient.eq
175	
176	/-- Two classes agreeing after restriction to a common refinement are equal; in
177	particular `mk` is invariant under restriction. -/
178	@[simp]
179	theorem mk_unitsRes {𝒰 𝒱 : X.PointedCover} (h : 𝒱 ≤ 𝒰) (a : X.unitsH1 𝒰) :
180	    mk 𝒱 (unitsRes h a) = mk 𝒰 a :=
181	  Quotient.sound ⟨𝒱, le_rfl, h, unitsRes_rfl _⟩
182	
183	private def mulSig (p q : Σ 𝒰 : X.PointedCover, X.unitsH1 𝒰) :
184	    Σ 𝒰 : X.PointedCover, X.unitsH1 𝒰 :=
185	  ⟨p.1 ⊓ q.1, unitsRes inf_le_left p.2 * unitsRes inf_le_right q.2⟩
186	
187	private lemma mulSig_compat {p p' q q' : Σ 𝒰 : X.PointedCover, X.unitsH1 𝒰}
188	    (hp : p ≈ p') (hq : q ≈ q') : mulSig p q ≈ mulSig p' q' := by
189	  obtain ⟨𝒲₁, h₁, h₂, e₁⟩ := hp
190	  obtain ⟨𝒲₂, h₃, h₄, e₂⟩ := hq
191	  refine ⟨𝒲₁ ⊓ 𝒲₂, inf_le_inf (inf_le_left.trans h₁) (inf_le_right.trans h₃),
192	    inf_le_inf (inf_le_left.trans h₂) (inf_le_right.trans h₄), ?_⟩
193	  have e₁' := congrArg (unitsRes (inf_le_left : 𝒲₁ ⊓ 𝒲₂ ≤ 𝒲₁)) e₁
194	  have e₂' := congrArg (unitsRes (inf_le_right : 𝒲₁ ⊓ 𝒲₂ ≤ 𝒲₂)) e₂
195	  simp only [unitsRes_unitsRes] at e₁' e₂'
196	  simp only [mulSig, map_mul, unitsRes_unitsRes]
197	  rw [e₁', e₂']
198	
199	instance : CommGroup X.CechPic where
200	  mul := Quotient.map₂ mulSig (fun _ _ hp _ _ hq ↦ mulSig_compat hp hq)
201	  one := mk ⊤ 1
202	  inv := Quotient.map (fun p ↦ ⟨p.1, p.2⁻¹⟩) (by
203	    rintro p p' ⟨𝒲, h₁, h₂, e⟩
204	    exact ⟨𝒲, h₁, h₂, by simp only [map_inv, e]⟩)
205	  mul_assoc a b c := by

### 2.3 The refinement colimit

```lean
/-- The definitional Picard group: Čech H¹ of the units presheaf, colimit over pointed covers. -/
def Scheme.CechPic (X : Scheme.{u}) : Type u :=
  Quot (fun p q : (Σ 𝒰 : X.PointedCover, PresheafOfGroups.H1 ⋯ 𝒰.opens) =>
    ∃ 𝒲, ∃ (h₁ : 𝒲 ≤ p.1) (h₂ : 𝒲 ≤ q.1), res h₁ p.2 = res h₂ q.2)
```

- The relation is an equivalence *because the poset is directed* (common refinement by pointwise
  `⊓`) and `res` strictly composes; the standard filtered-colimit argument is elementary and
  choice-free.
- Universe accounting: `X.PointedCover : Type u`, each `H1 … : Type u` (index `X : Type u`,
  values in `Type u`), the sigma is `Type u`, the quotient is `Type u`. **No `ULift` anywhere.**
- `CommGroup (X.CechPic)`: multiplication of classes represented on a common refinement;
  well-definedness from §2.2's `CommGroup (H1 …)` + `res` being a group hom.
- Constructor/eliminator API: `CechPic.mk (𝒰) (γ : OneCocycle …) : X.CechPic`,
  `CechPic.ind`, `CechPic.mk_eq_mk_iff_of_refines`, and the "sanity gate"
